correctness.rationale: Every positive rate pair with positive equilibrium has the unique inverse a=e p/[q(1-p)], b=f q/[p(1-q)] and ab=ef/[(1-p)(1-q)]>ef. The exact objective C(p,q) is coercive near the upper edges, and proportional reduction excludes any optimizer with both targets slack. On either binding edge the odds variable gives a strictly unimodal Az+B/z cost with one explicit optimum; unique corner transitions occur at the two stated radicals, ordered strictly by the positive radial derivative at the first threshold. The two constrained edge optima yield the complete global three-phase classification. Cooperative comparison proves global attraction from strictly positive states. Standard-library checker verifies 94057 finite assertions across 550 tested parameter sets, but analytic proof—not tests—covers the universally quantified claim.

value.rationale: Joint breeding and nonbreeding occupancy targets are meaningful conservation requirements; a linear colonization-intensity budget is a transparent idealized design problem. Exact all-parameter uniqueness and the three distinct resource-allocation regimes reveal target overshoot, explicit switching thresholds and the least cost, rather than merely reproducing an existing equilibrium formula or a numerical illustration. The result can be used as an exact benchmark for less idealized constrained conservation planning; it does not establish empirical optimality, discrete yearly probability feasibility or stochastic persistence guarantees.
